messages:
Arjun: Putting up a short runbook draft for spot/preemptible GPU drain handling + mixed pools. Want quick review before I drop it into the runbooks repo.

Maya: Nice — can you include exact k8s drain command and autoscaler caveats?

Arjun: Here[0m[0m[0m[0m (snippet):
```
kubectl cordon <node>
kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120
# prefer cordon then drain if cluster-autoscaler relies on node counts
```

Lisa: Add step: signal model-serving pods to flush KV caches and checkpoint tensor state. We saw OOMs when pods restarted mid-step.

Tony: Also document fallback routing: when spot capacity drops, route traffic to pinned reserved pool. Use routing policy `capacity_priority` and enforce per-model QoS.

Elena: We should include escalation path: if >30% of a spot pool drains in 10m, page SRE oncall and product infra owners. Include runbook snippet for paged escalation and slack incident channel.

Arjun: Draft includes a PromQL alert + small probe script. PromQL example: `sum by(pool) (increase(k8s_node_evictions_total[5m])) > 5` to trigger a high-drain alert. Probe script will attempt canary allocation and measure fallback latency.

Oncall-Bot: :rotating_light: alert: spot-drain-high (fired) — pool=us-west2-spot — evictions=12 in 5m — triggered by prom-rule `spot_drains_high`

Maya: For mixed pools, recommend target utilization 60-70% with a 20% spare buffer for bursty model serving. Document autoscaler scaling down cooldowns (recommend >= 5m) so we don't thrash.

Arjun: Adding sample smoke test to validate fallback routing:
```bash
# simulate reduced spot capacity by tainting nodes then exercise canary
kubectl taint nodes -l pool=spot gpu-preemptible=true:NoSchedule --overwrite
# run canary client: curl -XPOST https://canary.internal/models/serve -d '{"input":"test"}' -H 'x-canary: true'
# verify reserved pool picks up traffic and 95th latency < 400ms
```

Lisa: :thumbsup: Can you add who owns the cache flush hook? I can take it if you want.

Arjun: Assigning cache flush hook ownership to Lisa. Also adding cost note: mixed-pool saved ~38% TCO on recent batch runs, but add warning that latency-sensitive online models see minimal savings and need reserved capacity.

Tony: Add runbook checklist: expected behaviors, how to validate fallback, quick rollback (re-add nodes, remove taints, revert routing), and postmortem triggers. Keep TL;DR at the top for oncall.

Elena: LGTM — just add links to the runbook repo and the oncall run playbook (pagerduty) and a short note: do NOT rely on spot as single-zone critical. Also include contact list for infra/product owners.

Arjun: Thanks all — I'll push the updated draft in ~30m and create a follow-up PR in the runbooks repo. cc @Oncall-Bot so we can test the alert throttle in staging later tonight.
